listing.summary: Explore Sheep, Dog 'n' Wolf / Sheep, Dog 'n' Wolf: Rewooled (SDW-Community) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Prepare your original game
steps.instruction: For the managed direct-player route, copy your own original PC Sheep, Dog ’n’ Wolf game data into game-data beside SheepD3D.exe, with Levels directly inside game-data. Keep the original executable and DLLs in the source copy. The maintained --game-dir=game-data argument selects that folder; the game reads its saved rendering/input options. No engine compilation is needed. For external registration, supply your actual --game-dir=PATH in Change launch details, or use upstream’s SheepLauncher.exe workflow with its own installation.

presentation.manual_preparation: For the managed direct-player route, copy your own original PC Sheep, Dog ’n’ Wolf game data into game-data beside SheepD3D.exe, with Levels directly inside game-data. Keep the original executable and DLLs in the source copy. The maintained --game-dir=game-data argument selects that folder; the game reads its saved rendering/input options. No engine compilation is needed. For external registration, supply your actual --game-dir=PATH in Change launch details, or use upstream’s SheepLauncher.exe workflow with its own installation. The original game-data folder is declared for compatible runtime replacement and backup. Default saves and launcher/game options are stored in AppData/Infogrames/Sheep, Dog'n Wolf DX7, outside Portcove backups. Only the direct SheepD3D.exe is launched by the managed route; the optional launcher checks release pages rather than replacing the runtime. Upstream disc extraction, language export and custom data paths stay manual/external. Do not put converted/custom output over the version-owned player. Use external registration for customized launch workflows or SDW_SAVE_DIR. Existing external installations keep their files and runtime owner. Source/package inspection is separate from original-input, gameplay, minimum-environment and packaged Desktop acceptance observations.
